rules.source: Eric approved Acceptance material clock repair, reproduced on 1bec37d9, work order 2026-11-24 PR A.
rules.rule: Recognize the declared source/order only on the readiness read, material record and investment reminder close routes.
rules.initialization: The already guarded Acceptance runtime resolves the native route identity and applies its existing scene lock; no schema, configuration or frozen plan change.
rules.dateAndPermission: The existing signed UAT session, mixed-scope rejection and actual role checks still apply. The same time is observed by the UI read and occurrence validation. Untagged ordinary orders and production use wall time.
rules.expectation: On an actual adopted B order a simulated later-than-wall occurrence saves for the real follow-up role. An unbound order rejects the same valid-shaped time; another scene is refused and the two supported resource kinds retain original authority.

rules.source: Eric approved the existing 70-percent, idempotent native reminder and todo lifecycle on the same material basis, work order 2026-11-24 PR A.
rules.rule: Use the guarded clock for native material reminder selection, scan receipt, claim, current display and task timing.
rules.initialization: Keep the exact handover entry and event source key. Scanner receipt association now uses the original handover scope and authorized scene instead of expecting a generic rework todo.
rules.dateAndPermission: A guarded Pool owns the clock reader; the same transaction serves the notification candidate/open reads when present. Ordinary schedulers exclude clock-bound orders; only an existing signed actor claims a native eligible notice. Existing adopted policy, role eligibility and real receipt audit time are preserved.
rules.expectation: The first enabled 70-percent boundary emits exactly one receipt across repeat scans and two sessions. Read and close keep the pending task. Actual completion retains the historical lateness, original cutoff and adopted versions.

Isolated guarded Acceptance clock through its own canonical configuration. Real signed HTTP scope and native clock transitions remain covered.
